Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the call this morning — really helpful to understand Acme's live product use case. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of call:
- Primary goal: conversational product embedded in checkout flow (low-latency suggestions + streaming responses to the UI).
- Target TTFT: you mentioned ~300ms on web clients as a hard target for customer-facing interactions.
- Concurrency/throughput: typical concurrency ~50-100 concurrent users, with up to 300 concurrent during peak promotions; sustained throughput estimate ~20 req/s per region with short bursts to 100+ req/s.
- Streaming: prefer SSE on web for simplicity; willing to consider WebSocket for lower round-trip overhead. Chunk cadence: want smooth incremental UI updates (roughly 200-400ms per chunk).
- Security/compliance: SOC2 and standard data retention controls required — Priya will share the procurement checklist.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll loop in Neha (solutions) and Marcus (sales manager) to validate TTFT targets and give recommended deployment options (hosted vs. dedicated) and expected percentile numbers.
2) Please send a representative prompt payload and avg token lengths so we can run a perf estimate.
3) We’ll provide a short perf doc + a one-off test run on a mirrored workload and share P50/P95/P99 TTFT + recommended streaming config.

Attachments: SLO-template.pdf (short template for filling in final SLOs).

If anything above is off, call it out — otherwise we’ll proceed with next-step #1.

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 300ms TTFT is our customer-facing goal on desktop/web with SSE. We can tolerate up to ~500ms for large-model fallbacks, but need P95 under 450ms if possible.
- For mobile the target is looser (~400ms) because of network variance.
- Our typical request payload is ~120 tokens input and we expect ~45 tokens output on average for the suggestion flow.
- Concurrency note: 50-100 normal, but during flash sales we’ve seen short spikes to ~350 concurrent sessions hitting the suggestion endpoint. We care about graceful degradation (fallback to shorter responses or reduced sampling) rather than hard failures.

Priya will drop the procurement checklist by end of day. For the perf run, can you run both an SSE and WebSocket streaming test so we can compare chunk cadence and TTFT behaviour? We’re especially interested in P50/P95/P99 for TTFT and chunk-to-chunk latency (i.e., how fast the first chunk arrives and how regularly subsequent chunks arrive).

Appreciate it — happy to jump on a follow-up call if Neha wants to walk through the workload.

— Alex

Hi all — quick technical answers and recommended plan. TL;DR: we can meet their goals with the right deployment and a short benchmarking pass.

Host vs Dedicated (high level):
- Hosted API: good for fast time-to-value. For a payload of ~120 in / ~45 out, expected TTFT (hosted) for medium-size open models: P50 ~120-220ms, P95 ~280-420ms, P99 ~500-750ms depending on model and region. Streaming SSE chunk cadence (hosted): first chunk 110-220ms, subsequent chunks ~150-350ms.
- Redwood Dedicated: lower and more predictable TTFT because of reserved GPU pools and tuned kernels. Expect P50 ~80-160ms, P95 ~160-300ms, P99 ~300-450ms for the same model, with chunk cadence tighter (~100-200ms per chunk). Dedicated also gives better headroom for spikes and predictable concurrency.

SSE vs WebSocket:
- SSE is simpler to integrate for web UIs and works well for most cases. WebSocket typically has slightly lower handshake overhead and better control for bidirectional flows; if you need sub-100ms TTFT consistently, prefer WebSocket on dedicated infra.

Chunk cadence & size suggestions:
- Aim for first chunk within 150-300ms for web.
- Target chunk cadence 150-350ms to keep UI responsive without sending lots of tiny updates. For Acme’s expected output length (~45 tokens), 2-4 chunks is typical.
- Configure server-side generation to flush after ~12-16 tokens or when a punctuation boundary is reached to balance freshness vs. overhead.

Concurrency/throughput guidance:
- For 50-100 concurrent users with bursts to 350, we recommend Dedicated if Acme needs strict SLOs (P95 <=450ms) and graceful degradation during spikes. Hosted can meet targets most of the time but can show variability during noisy neighbors or cross-region load.
- Autoscaling + burst capacity on Dedicated gives controlled behavior: keep a reserve for 20-30% headroom during known promotions.

Fallbacks under overload:
- Short-term: return shorter responses (truncate to top-k or reduce max tokens), or switch to cached common responses.
- Medium-term: degrade to a compact model variant for faster TTFT. We can automate model variant routing with a policy.

Next steps (proposed):
1) Acme to provide representative payloads and a worst-case traffic profile (spikes).
2) We’ll run a 2-hour perf test (hosted + dedicated mirror) and return P50/P95/P99 TTFT, first-chunk latency, and chunk cadence metrics.
3) Deliver a filled SLO template and a short recommendation memo (hosted vs dedicated + config).

I attached a quick perf estimate workbook (perf-estimate-ACME-20260621.xlsx) with ballpark capacity numbers. If helpful we can also set up a 30-45 minute technical deep-dive to walk through the test plan.

-Neha
